_note: Unity-specific consumer settings. Nothing in sources/derive/ reads this file. These are the conventions and fudges that used to be baked into the data layer; they live here because they are properties of one consumer, not of the survey.

terrain.note: TerrainData encodes height as unsigned 16-bit normalised over [y_base, y_base + y_size] metres. auto derives ONE window for the whole site from terrain_manifest.range_m plus auto_margin_m, so every tile shares it (seamless neighbours) and nothing can be clipped; 16-bit over even a 150 m window is ~2 mm. Set numbers to pin a window -- the adapter still refuses to encode ground that falls outside it.
terrain.cliffs_note: The data holds cliff faces at 65-80 degrees (measured on the EA DTM at Cliftonville: 5 m wide for a 10 m drop, 8.6 m in one cell at the steepest). If cliffs render as ~45 degree ramps, the engine did it, not the data. Keep heightmapResolution equal to grid_res (513 for a 512 m tile = 1 m), never let an importer resample, and set Terrain Pixel Error to 1-2: the default 5 decimates steep geometry at distance. terrain_manifest.slope_qa tells you what steepness went in.

class_lift_m._note: Draw-order lift so a service road meeting a trunk road loses the depth test instead of z-fighting. Purely a rendering hack; it is not survey data and must not travel with it.

roads.offset_note: Invented deck/bore offsets. OSM gives no structure height, so these are a look, not a measurement -- which is exactly why they belong to the consumer.
